column1: # Phase 230 (D-23): the honest-skip set, as data.
# `ci-gate` counts a `skipped` conclusion as a pass, so "this lane was skipped" is
# indistinguishable from "this lane passed" unless the legitimate skips are enumerated
# somewhere a machine can read. That enumeration used to live only as prose in
# MAINTAINING.md. Prose is now a RENDERER of this file, not a second source of truth:
# manifest <=> ci.yml <=> MAINTAINING.md and fails in every direction (an undocumented
# demotion, a stale doc entry, or a manifest row naming a construct ci.yml does not have).
#   - Phase 231 GATE-03                                    SHOULD read this file rather
#   A  event-gated, pre-existing (Phase 196). NOT demoted by Phase 230. Phase 231's
#      GATE-01/GATE-02 own these; the observer deliberately does NOT assert on them --
#      asserting would add a tenth red to a 0-pass/9-fail nightly, which is the
#      unread-noise failure this milestone exists to remove.
#   B  event-gated, demoted BY Phase 230. These are exactly what AFTER-PUSH must observe
#   C  diff-gated (docs-only). Skips on the CONTENT of the diff rather than the event --
#      a different audit question from A/B.
# COLUMNS (TAB-separated; `#` and blank lines are comments)
#   id             the ci.yml job id, or the step `id:` when kind=step. Every id here
#                  MUST resolve in ci.yml -- the parity guard asserts it, which is what
#                  stops this file from drifting into fiction.
#   parent_job_id  owning job id when kind=step; `-` when kind=job. A step row's parent
#                  MUST also appear here as a kind=job row -- that is how the observer
#                  resolves the parent's display_name (the Actions API returns names,
#   display_name   the job `name:` / step `name:` EXACTLY as ci.yml spells it. The
#                  parity guard pins id and display_name adjacent in ci.yml so the
#                  API-facing lookup cannot rot independently of the id-facing guard.
#   gate_level     job | step -- WHERE the predicate is applied. For the four
#                  ruleset-required tier-C lanes this MUST stay `step`: a job-level
#                  docs_only gate would make the required context `skipped` and can
#   gate           the literal gating predicate, normalized (${{ }} stripped, whitespace
#                    assert = must have executed on a non-PR run (tier B only)
#                    exempt = event-gated but ALSO outcome-gated, so a skip on a healthy
#                    ignore = outside the observer's scope (tier A / tier C)
